quick-start.title: zoxide Quick Start
quick-start.excerpt: Get started with zoxide in 5 minutes, learn basic commands and configuration methods.
quick-start.content:
# zoxide Quick Start Guide

zoxide is a smart directory jumper written in Rust. Get started in minutes.

## Install zoxide

### macOS
```bash
brew install zoxide
```

### Windows
```powershell
scoop install zoxide
```

### Linux / all platforms
```bash
cargo install zoxide
```

## Shell configuration

Add initialization to your shell config and reload.

#### zsh
```bash
eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"
```

#### bash
```bash
eval "$(zoxide init bash)"
```

#### fish
```fish
zoxide init fish | source
```

#### PowerShell
```powershell
Invoke-Expression (& { (zoxide init powershell | Out-String) })
```

## Basic usage

```bash
# Jump to a matching directory
z project

# Interactive fuzzy pick
zi pro

# Go back
z -

# List matches
z -l project
```

zoxide learns your habits and makes directory navigation fast and fuzzy.

basic-commands.title: zoxide Basic Commands
basic-commands.excerpt: Learn all basic zoxide commands and usage tips in depth.
basic-commands.content:
# zoxide Basic Commands

Key commands you need every day.

## z - smart jump
```bash
z project
z proj       # partial name
z src/main   # path fragments
```
zoxide ranks results by relevance and frequency.

## zi - interactive selection
```bash
zi project
```
Use arrow keys to pick, Enter to jump.

## z - - go back
```bash
z docs
z -          # back to previous
```

## z -l - list matches
```bash
z -l project
```

## Tips
- Combine: `z -l proj` then `z proj`
- Pipe results: `z -l test | head -5`

# Shell Configuration Guide

Configure zoxide in your favorite shell.

## zsh
```bash
eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"
```

## bash
```bash

```

### macOS bash profile
```bash
if [ -f ~/.bashrc ]; then
    source ~/.bashrc
fi
```

## fish
```fish
zoxide init fish | source
```

## PowerShell
```powershell
Invoke-Expression (& { (zoxide init powershell | Out-String) })
```

## Verify
```bash

z ~
```

If command not found: check install, config file, and reload the shell.

advanced-config.title: zoxide Advanced Configuration
advanced-config.excerpt: Learn zoxide's advanced configuration options, including environment variables, custom aliases, directory exclusion, and more.
advanced-config.content:
# zoxide Advanced Configuration

Customize zoxide with env vars, aliases, and performance tweaks.

## Environment Variables

### Exclude directories
```bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var:/node_modules"
```
Separate multiple paths with colons.

### Custom database location
```bash
export _ZO_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.local/share/zoxide"
```

### Maximum history age
```bash
export _ZO_MAXAGE=5000
```

### Exclusion patterns
```bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_PATHS=".git"
```

## Alias Settings
```bash
alias zz='z'
alias zi='zi'
alias za='zoxide add'
alias zq='zoxide query'
alias zr='zoxide remove'
```

## fzf Integration
```bash
# Add to ~/.zshrc
zi() {
  local dir
  dir=$(zoxide query -l | fzf) && z "$dir"
}
```

## Performance Optimization

### Reduce index scope
```bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var:/proc:/sys"
```

### Periodic cleanup
```bash
ls -lh ~/.zo
rm ~/.zo
```

## Team Collaboration
```bash
export _ZO_DATA_DIR="/shared/path/zoxide"
```

## Summary
Start with exclusions, then fine-tune history and database location to fit your workflow. See the official docs for more options.

fzf-integration.title: zoxide and fzf Integration
fzf-integration.excerpt: Learn how to combine zoxide with fzf to achieve more powerful directory search and selection.
fzf-integration.content:
# zoxide and fzf Integration

Combine zoxide with fzf for powerful fuzzy selection of directories.

## What is fzf-
- Fuzzy search for files and directories
- Interactive selection with preview
- Highly customizable

## Installing fzf

### macOS
```bash
brew install fzf
```

### Linux
```bash
# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install fzf

# Arch Linux
sudo pacman -S fzf
```

### Manual install
```bash
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/junegunn/fzf.git ~/.fzf
~/.fzf/install
```

## Basic Integration

### Use fzf to pick a zoxide result
```bash
# zsh/bash
zi() {
    local dir
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | fzf) && z "$dir"
}
```

### fish version
```fish
function zi
    set dir (zoxide query -l | fzf)
    if test -n "$dir"
        z "$dir"
    end
end
```

## Advanced Integration

### Add preview
```bash
zi() {
    local dir
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | fzf --preview 'ls -la {}') && z "$dir"
}
```

### Multi-select
```bash
zi() {
    local dirs
    dirs=$(zoxide query -l | fzf -m)
    if [ -n "$dirs" ]; then
        echo "$dirs" | while read dir; do
            echo "Selected: $dir"
        done
    fi
}
```

## Practical functions

### Jump with preview
```bash
zfp() {
    local dir
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | fzf --preview 'tree -L 2 {}')
    [ -n "$dir" ] && z "$dir" && ls -la
}
```

### Search and open editor
```bash
zcode() {
    local dir
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | fzf)
    [ -n "$dir" ] && z "$dir" && code .
}
```

### Search then run a command
```bash
zexec() {
    local dir cmd
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | fzf)
    if [ -n "$dir" ]; then
        z "$dir"
        read -p "Enter command: " cmd
        eval "$cmd"
    fi
}
```

## fzf Configuration

### Custom theme
```bash
export FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS='
  --color=fg:#f8f8f2,bg:#282a36,hl:#bd93f9
  --color=fg+:#f8f8f2,bg+:#44475a,hl+:#bd93f9
  --color=info:#ffb86c,prompt:#50fa7b,pointer:#ff79c6
  --color=marker:#ff79c6,spinner:#ffb86c,header:#6272a4
'
```

### Custom preview command
```bash
export FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS="--preview 'tree -C {} | head -20'"
```

## Real-World Use

### Quick project switching
```bash
zp() {
    local dir
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | grep -i project | fzf)
    [ -n "$dir" ] && z "$dir"
}
```

### Recent directories
```bash
zr() {
    local dir
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | sort -k2 -rn | fzf)
    [ -n "$dir" ] && z "$dir"
}
```

### Filter by type (git repos)
```bash
zgit() {
    local dir
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | xargs -I {} sh -c 'test -d {}/.git && echo {}' | fzf)
    [ -n "$dir" ] && z "$dir"
}
```

## Performance Tips

- Limit results: `head -50`
- Use lighter previews when data is large

```bash
zi() {
    local dir
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | head -50 | fzf)
    [ -n "$dir" ] && z "$dir"
}
```

```bash
zi() {
    local dir
    dir=$(zoxide query -l | fzf --bind 'change:reload:zoxide query -l {q}') && z "$dir"
}
```

## Troubleshooting

If you see `fzf: command not found`:
1. Verify installation
2. Ensure `fzf` is in PATH
3. Reload your shell config

## Best Practices
1. Use previews when helpful, not always
2. Limit result count for large datasets
3. Make aliases for your common workflows

## Next Steps
- [Troubleshooting](/tutorials/troubleshooting)
- [Performance Optimization](/tutorials/performance)
- [Advanced Configuration Tips](/tutorials/advanced-config)

performance.title: zoxide Performance Optimization
performance.excerpt: Learn how to optimize zoxide's performance, including database optimization, startup speed improvements, and more.
performance.content:
# zoxide Performance Optimization

This guide shows how to tune zoxide for speed: smaller databases, faster startup, and snappy queries.

## Database Optimization

### Exclude unnecessary directories
Keep noise out of the index:
```bash
# System and temp paths
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var:/proc:/sys"

# Add development dependencies if you have many projects
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var:/node_modules:/.git"
```

Benefits:
- Smaller database
- Faster queries
- Lower memory

### Clean the database regularly
```bash
# Check database size
ls -lh ~/.zo

# If it grows too large, rebuild it (zoxide will relearn)
rm ~/.zo
```

### Limit history
```bash
# Keep roughly one year of history
export _ZO_MAXAGE=365
```

## Startup Speed

### Lazy initialization (zsh example)
```bash
zoxide() {
    unfunction zoxide
    eval "$(command zoxide init zsh)"
    zoxide "$@"
}
```

### Place init at the end of your rc file
```bash
# ~/.zshrc
eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"
```

## Query Optimization

- Prefer precise keywords: `z my-project` instead of `z pro`
- Use the access frequency zoxide learns automatically

## Memory Optimization
```bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var:/proc:/sys:/node_modules"
export _ZO_MAXAGE=1000
```

## Performance Testing
```bash
# Measure init time
time eval "$(zoxide init zsh)"

# Measure a query
time z project
```

## Real-World Cases

### Many projects
```bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/node_modules:/.git:/dist:/build"
```

### Sysadmin
```bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var:/proc:/sys:/usr"
export _ZO_DATA_DIR="$HOME/.local/share/zoxide"
```

### Team collaboration
```bash
export _ZO_DATA_DIR="/shared/zoxide"
```

## Monitoring
```bash
# Weekly size check via cron
0 0 * * 0 ls -lh ~/.zo >> ~/zoxide-size.log
```

```bash
# cleanup-zoxide.sh
#!/bin/bash
ZO_DB="$HOME/.zo"
MAX_SIZE=10485760  # 10MB
if [ -f "$ZO_DB" ]; then
    SIZE=$(stat -f%z "$ZO_DB" 2>/dev/null || stat -c%s "$ZO_DB" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ "$SIZE" -gt "$MAX_SIZE" ]; then
        echo "Database too large, backing up and resetting..."
        cp "$ZO_DB" "$ZO_DB.backup"
        rm "$ZO_DB"
    fi
fi
```

## Best Practices
1. Exclude noisy directories first
2. Clean up occasionally
3. Limit history if needed
4. Keep init near the end of your rc file
5. Monitor database size and tweak

## Next Steps
- [fzf Integration](/tutorials/fzf-integration)
- [Troubleshooting](/tutorials/troubleshooting)
- [Advanced Configuration Tips](/tutorials/advanced-config)

troubleshooting.title: zoxide Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.excerpt: Solve common problems when using zoxide, including installation issues, configuration problems, performance issues, etc.
troubleshooting.content:
# zoxide Troubleshooting

Common issues and quick fixes.

## Install issues
- `zoxide: command not found`: ensure install and PATH.
```bash
which zoxide
zoxide --version
echo $PATH
```

## Config not applied
- Confirm init lines exist and reload shell.
```bash
source ~/.zshrc   # or bashrc / fish config
```

## Wrong jump
- Use interactive list:
```bash
zi project
z -l project
```
- Manually add:
```bash
zoxide add /path/to/dir
```

## Database issues
```bash
ls -lh ~/.zo
cp ~/.zo ~/.zo.backup
rm ~/.zo          # rebuild if corrupted/too big
```

## Startup too slow
- Try lazy loading for zsh:
```bash
zoxide() {
    unfunction zoxide
    eval "$(command zoxide init zsh)"
    zoxide "$@"
}
```
- Place init near end of rc file.

## Query slow
```bash
export _ZO_EXCLUDE_DIRS="/tmp:/var:/node_modules"
export _ZO_MAXAGE=1000
```

## Windows path issues
Use PowerShell init:
```powershell
Invoke-Expression (& { (zoxide init powershell | Out-String) })
```

## Debug
```bash
export _ZO_DEBUG=1
z project
```

zoxide-vs-autojump.title: zoxide vs autojump Performance Comparison
zoxide-vs-autojump.excerpt: Detailed comparison of the performance differences and user experience between zoxide and autojump.
zoxide-vs-autojump.author: zoxide.org
zoxide-vs-autojump.content:
# zoxide vs autojump Performance Comparison

zoxide and autojump are both directory jumpers, but their speed and features differ.

## Performance
- Startup: **zoxide ~5ms** vs **autojump ~50ms**
- Query: zoxide fuzzy search < 10ms; autojump 20-50ms in large trees

## Features
- Fuzzy search: zoxide - / autojump -
- Interactive selection (`zi`): zoxide - / autojump -
- Learning: zoxide smart weighting; autojump basic frequency

## Usability
```bash
# zoxide
z project

# autojump
j project
```

Config: zoxide needs one init command; autojump requires extra shell setup.

## Cross-platform
- zoxide: macOS, Linux, Windows
- autojump: macOS, Linux (limited Windows)

## Conclusion
Choose zoxide for speed and modern UX. Migration is straightforward if you currently use autojump. See the [full comparison](/comparisons).
